brief.headline: Push cap price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc (market says possible at volume) and move payment to 15 days to free up ₹2.39 L cash for us.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a price cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on the 28 mm induction-wad PP cap.
priceAsk.basis: The open market says ₹0.85–0.95/pc is typical, but ₹0.65–0.80/pc is doable at higher volume or looser spec — we're already spending ₹58.17 L a year with them, so press for that better rate.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹2.39 L cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: This supplier publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or debt. That means we lean on our own purchase data and the backups we've lined up. We spend ₹58.17 L a year with them — a solid order book — so they'll want to keep us. But without visibility into their health, don't squeeze so hard that a fragile supplier walks away; instead, use the threat of a second source to get the price and payment moves.

evidence.point: Our annual spend with them is material enough to matter to a private converter.
The open market says a 28 mm PP cap typically runs ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume or looser spec.
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask band; ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical; ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: Paying 15 days earlier frees up cash for us.
HDPE resin import price is a public cost benchmark for rigid plastics.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100). Top second-source candidate if we need to split the business.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); revenue ₹946.50 Cr, health score B (73/100). Strong and profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Pan-India manufacturer of plastics — a maker source that could bypass converter margin if we can meet their volume thresholds.

risks: They publish no financials, so we can't tell if they're healthy or stretched — don't push so hard that a weak supplier exits and leaves us scrambling.
Moving payment from 30 days to 15 days tightens their cash — pair it with a volume commitment or longer contract so they see upside, not just a squeeze.
Market backups are leads, not qualified suppliers — start the paperwork now (audit, sample, trial) so we have a real second source in 3–6 months.
Our current payment terms (30 days after receipt) aren't the worst we give anyone, so they may resist going shorter unless we sweeten the deal with volume or a price they can live with.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing your cap price in line with the ₹0.65–0.80 band the market supports at volume, and moving to 15-day payment to free up working cash for both of us.
